completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.hasSum_fourierExpCoeff_mul_conj
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.8.6_2 (Parseval's formula for two functions, exponential form): for `f`, `g`
square integrable on `[-π, π]`, `(2π)⁻¹ ∫_{-π}^{π} f(x) ḡ(x) dx = ∑_{n ∈ ℤ} c_n c̄'_n`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.hasSum_fourierCosSinCoeff_mul_conj
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.8.6_1 (Parseval's formula for two functions, trigonometric form): for `f`, `g`
square integrable on `[-π, π]`,
`π⁻¹ ∫_{-π}^{π} f(x) ḡ(x) dx = ½ a_0 ā'_0 + ∑_{n ≥ 1} (a_n ā'_n + b_n b̄'_n)`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierCoeff_isLittleO
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.8.7: if `f` has period `2π` and `f^{(m)}` is piecewise continuous, then
`a_n, b_n, c_n = o(n^{-m})` as `n → ∞`. Special case: `f` is assumed `C^m` (so `f^{(m)}` is
continuous).

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.eq_of_fourierCoeff_eq
completed.doc:
DLMF §1.8(i) (uniqueness of Fourier series): continuous `2π`-periodic functions with the
same Fourier coefficients `a_n`, `b_n` are equal.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.hasSum_exp_neg_sq_mul
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.8.16: for `ℜω > 0`,
`∑_{n ∈ ℤ} e^{-(n+x)²ω} = √(π/ω) (1 + 2 ∑_{n ≥ 1} e^{-n²π²/ω} cos(2nπx))`, with the principal
square root. Stronger than DLMF: `x` may be complex. The special case `f(x) = e^{-ωx²}` of
1.8.14; compare Mathlib's `Complex.tsum_exp_neg_quadratic`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.laplaceTransform_exp_neg_sub_exp_neg_div
completed.doc:
DLMF Table 1.14.4, row 14: `(e^{-bt} - e^{-at})/t ↦ ln((s + a)/(s + b))`, `ℜs > -ℜa`,
`ℜs > -ℜb`, principal logarithm.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.laplaceTransform_one_sub_cosh_div
completed.doc:
DLMF Table 1.14.4, row 15: `2(1 - cosh(at))/t ↦ ln(1 - a²/s²)`, under the **corrected**
condition `ℜs > |ℜa|` (DLMF prints `ℜ(s + a) > 0`, insufficient since the left side is even in
`a`).

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.laplaceTransform_one_sub_cos_div
completed.doc:
DLMF Table 1.14.4, row 16: `2(1 - cos(at))/t ↦ ln(1 + a²/s²)`, `ℜs > |ℑa|` (DLMF:
`ℜs > 0`, for real `a`).

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.laplaceTransform_sin_div
completed.doc:
DLMF Table 1.14.4, row 17: `sin(at)/t ↦ arctan(a/s)`, `ℜs > |ℑa|` (DLMF: `ℜs > 0`, for real
`a`), principal branch.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integral_mul_comp_mul_eq_mellin
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.36 (Parseval-type formula): if `x^{-σ} f(x)` and `x^{σ-1} g(x)` are absolutely
integrable on `(0, ∞)` and `𝓜(g)(σ + it)` or `𝓜(f)(1 - σ - it)` is absolutely integrable, then
for `y > 0`, `∫₀^∞ f(x) g(yx) dx = (1/2πi) ∫_{σ-i∞}^{σ+i∞} y^{-s} 𝓜(f)(1 - s) 𝓜(g)(s) ds`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.integral_sq_eq_mellin
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.14.38 (Mellin–Parseval): for real `f` with `x^{-1/2} f(x)` absolutely integrable on
`(0, ∞)` and `𝓜(f)(½ + it)` absolutely integrable,
`∫₀^∞ (f(x))² dx = (1/2π) ∫ |𝓜(f)(½ + it)|² dt`.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.integrableOn_powKernel_mul_rpow_iff
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.6.36: for `x > 0`, `μ > 0`, `0 < α ≤ 1` and `s = 0, 1, 2, …`, the convolution
integral `∫₀^x (x-t)^{μ-1} t^{-s-α} dt` exists in the usual (Lebesgue) sense exactly when
`s = 0` and `α < 1`.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.not_integrableOn_rpow_div_add
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.6.3: the termwise integrals `∫₀^∞ t^{-s-1/3}/(x+t) dt`, `s = 1, 2, …`, diverge
(here: the integrand is not integrable on `(0, ∞)`), for every `x > 0`.

completed.name: DLMF.AsymptoticApproximations.watson_lemma_log
completed.doc:
DLMF 2.3.9: Watson's lemma with a logarithmic factor. Under the hypotheses of 2.3.8, and if
`e^{-ct} q(t) ln t` is also integrable on `(0, ∞)`,
`∫₀^∞ e^{-xt} q(t) ln t dt ∼ ∑ Γ'((s+λ)/μ) aₛ x^{-(s+λ)/μ} - (ln x) ∑ Γ((s+λ)/μ) aₛ x^{-(s+λ)/μ}`
as `x → +∞`, in the sense that the remainder after `N` terms of both sums is
`O(x^{-(N+λ)/μ} ln x)`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierCoeff_lift_eq_fourierExpCoeff
newHelpers.doc:
The Fourier coefficients of the periodic lift to the circle agree with the
DLMF exponential coefficients on `[-π, π]`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierExpCoeff_eq_fourier_indicator
newHelpers.doc:
The exponential Fourier coefficients are the Fourier transform of the function
restricted to a period, with the frequency and integral normalization rescaled.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.tendsto_fourierExpCoeff_comp
newHelpers.doc:
The exponential Fourier coefficients vanish along any sequence of integer
frequencies escaping finite sets; no convergence assumption is needed for totalized integrals.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierExpCoeff_deriv
newHelpers.doc:
Differentiation of a continuously differentiable periodic function multiplies
its nonzero Fourier coefficients by `in`. This is Mathlib's integration-by-parts formula.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierExpCoeff_iteratedDeriv
newHelpers.doc:
Repeated differentiation multiplies each nonzero Fourier coefficient by `(in)^m`.
Periodicity of derivatives is supplied by TauCeti's `Function.Periodic.deriv`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.fourierExpCoeff_mul_nat_isLittleO
newHelpers.doc:
Along any nonzero integer multiple of the natural frequencies, a `C^m` periodic
function has coefficients `o(n⁻ᵐ)`.

newHelpers.name: integrableOn_exp_neg_mul_rpow_sub_one_mul_log
newHelpers.doc:
The logarithmic Gamma integrand is absolutely integrable for positive order
and positive exponential decay.

newHelpers.name: integral_exp_neg_mul_rpow_sub_one_mul_log
newHelpers.doc:
The logarithmic exponential moment equals
`x⁻ˢ (Γ'(s) - log x Γ(s))` for positive order and Laplace parameter.

newHelpers.name: integrableOn_exp_neg_mul_sum_rpow_mul_log
newHelpers.doc:
A finite sum of logarithmic Gamma kernels is integrable against positive
exponential decay.

newHelpers.name: integral_exp_neg_mul_sum_rpow_mul_log
newHelpers.doc:
Integrating a finite logarithmic power expansion gives the corresponding
Gamma-derivative coefficients.

newHelpers.name: isBigO_integral_exp_mul_log
newHelpers.doc:
A Laplace transform of a logarithmically weighted remainder has a power bound
if the unweighted remainder has any strictly higher order at zero.

newHelpers.name: isBigO_log_gamma_term
newHelpers.doc: A logarithmic Gamma moment has the order `x⁻ˢ log x` at infinity.

newHelpers.name: isBigO_integral_exp_mul_log_sub_sum
newHelpers.doc:
Watson's lemma with a logarithmic factor for a strictly increasing sequence
of positive exponents. An extra term of the input expansion absorbs the logarithm in
the remainder, so no differentiation of an asymptotic error estimate is needed.

newHelpers.name: hasSum_fourierCoeff_mul_conj
newHelpers.doc:
The products of the Fourier coefficients of two square-integrable functions on
the circle sum to their integral pairing, with normalized Haar measure.

newHelpers.name: hasSum_fourierCoeffOn_mul_conj
newHelpers.doc:
Parseval's pairing on an interval: the products of the Fourier coefficients
sum to the integral pairing divided by the interval length.

newHelpers.name: Complex.summable_exp_quadratic
newHelpers.doc:
A complex quadratic exponential with negative real leading coefficient is
absolutely summable on the integers.

newHelpers.name: Real.ae_fourierInv_fourier_eq
newHelpers.doc:
Fourier inversion holds almost everywhere when both the function and its
Fourier transform are integrable.

newHelpers.name: Real.integral_mul_eq_integral_fourier_neg_mul
newHelpers.doc:
The bilinear Parseval identity for integrable functions, assuming the Fourier
transform of the second function is integrable.

newHelpers.name: Real.integral_mul_eq_integral_fourier_neg_mul_of_or
newHelpers.doc:
The bilinear Parseval identity needs absolute integrability of either Fourier
transform, in addition to integrability of both original functions.

newHelpers.name: Real.integral_fourier_mul_eq_flip
newHelpers.doc: The bilinear Fourier pairing can be interchanged for two integrable functions.

newHelpers.name: Real.integral_fourierInv_mul_eq_flip
newHelpers.doc: The inverse Fourier pairing can be interchanged for two integrable functions.

newHelpers.name: Complex.re_segment_ge_min
newHelpers.doc:
A segment between right-half-plane points remains a positive distance from
the imaginary axis.

newHelpers.name: Complex.integral_segment_exp_neg_mul
newHelpers.doc:
Integrating an exponential over the parameter segment removes the apparent
singularity of the exponential difference divided by the integration variable.

newHelpers.name: Complex.integrable_segment_exp_neg_mul
newHelpers.doc:
The two-variable exponential kernel is integrable over a finite parameter
segment and the positive half-line.

newHelpers.name: Complex.integral_segment_inv
newHelpers.doc:
The integral of the reciprocal along a segment in the right half-plane is
the difference of the principal logarithms of the endpoints.

newHelpers.name: Complex.integrableOn_exp_sub_exp_div
newHelpers.doc:
An exponential difference divided by the variable is absolutely integrable
when both exponential parameters lie in the right half-plane.

newHelpers.name: Complex.integral_exp_sub_exp_div_eq_log_sub
newHelpers.doc:
Complex exponential Frullani's formula in the right half-plane, expressed as
a difference of principal logarithms.

newHelpers.name: Complex.log_div_of_re_pos
newHelpers.doc:
Division of two right-half-plane points subtracts their principal logarithms;
the difference of their arguments stays strictly between `-π` and `π`.

newHelpers.name: Complex.integral_exp_sub_exp_div
newHelpers.doc:
Complex exponential Frullani's formula with the principal logarithm of the
ratio, valid for arbitrary right-half-plane parameters.

newHelpers.name: Complex.log_one_sub_sq
newHelpers.doc:
The principal logarithm factors `1-z²` into `1-z` and `1+z` whenever both
linear factors avoid the branch cut. Their imaginary parts have opposite signs.

newHelpers.name: Complex.VerticalIntegrable.mellin_comp_mul_left
newHelpers.doc:
Positive dilation preserves absolute integrability of a Mellin transform on
a fixed vertical line.

newHelpers.name: mellin_conj
newHelpers.doc:
Complex conjugation commutes with the Mellin transform after conjugating the
exponent, since the integration variable is positive real.

newHelpers.name: mellin_vertical_eq_fourier
newHelpers.doc:
The weighted function in logarithmic coordinates has Fourier transform equal
to the Mellin transform on a vertical line, with frequency scaled by `2π`.

newHelpers.name: MellinConvergent.integrable_log_weight
newHelpers.doc:
Absolute Mellin convergence gives integrability of the real weighted function
in logarithmic coordinates.

newHelpers.name: integral_mul_eq_mellin_parseval
newHelpers.doc:
Mellin Parseval's bilinear identity with absolute convergence on complementary
vertical lines and an integrable transform on either line.
